# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✌ 🤟 ☝ 👏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆]

I am Deaf. I see the bomb: Display [0], Light [red], Wires 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red].

I received gestures from Mute and Blind, but I cannot interpret them without a shared context or manual knowledge which I do not have. However, my primary role is to convey visual information to those who can hear (Blind) or read (Mute).

Since I cannot hear, I must speak to inform Blind of the visual state, as he is the one who acts. He needs to know what he is touching versus what is displayed.

The most critical visual data for a defusal scenario usually involves wire colors and display numbers. I will describe the scene clearly to Blind so he can correlate his tactile input with the visual reality. I will also acknowledge Mute's attempt to communicate by providing the raw data they might need to cross-reference with their manual.

To Blind (who can hear me):
"The bomb has a digital display showing '0'. There is a red light on. There are three wires: Wire 1 is Yellow, Wire 2 is Green, Wire 3 is Red."

To Mute (who can read my speech? No, Mute cannot speak or touch, but can read manual. Mute receives speech? The rules say 'When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.' So Mute hears me too? Wait. 'Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words'. Mute is named 'Mute' because he cannot *speak*. Can he hear? The table says Mute 'Cannot Speak, or touch the bomb'. It does not say he cannot hear. Deaf 'Cannot Hear anything'. Blind 'Cannot See'. So Mute can likely hear. If Mute can hear, he gets my description. If Mute can read gestures, he gets my gestures.

Let's assume standard roles:
Deaf: Sees, Cannot Hear. Speaks/Gestures out. Receives Gestures/Text? No, "You never receive speech." But I receive gestures.
Mute: Reads Manual, Cannot Speak. Likely Hears and Sees? Or just Hears? Table: Mute "Read the manual". Usually implies seeing text. But in these puzzles, Mute often hears. Let's look at channels. "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." This implies Mute CAN HEAR. "When you gesture, Mute receives it." This implies Mute CAN SEE.
So Mute sees and hears.
Blind: Touches. Cannot See. Receives Speech. Does he receive gestures? "Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol". Blind cannot see. So Blind gets blanks from gestures.
Deaf: Sees. Cannot Hear. Receives Gestures. Does Deaf receive speech? "You never receive speech."

Okay, strategy:
1. Describe visual state to Blind (via speech) so he knows what to cut/touch.
2. Describe visual state to Mute (via speech) so he can check against manual.
3. Since I don't know the manual, I provide the facts.

I will speak to everyone (default) describing the bomb.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is red.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb state remains unchanged: Display [0], Light [red], Wires 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red].

I received a gesture from Mute: [✌]. Since I am Deaf, I cannot hear speech, but I can see gestures. However, without a pre-established code or manual knowledge (which I don't have), this symbol is ambiguous to me. It could mean "two", "peace", "victory", or something specific to the manual.

My primary duty is to ensure Blind (who acts) and Mute (who knows the manual) have accurate visual information. Blind needs to know what he is touching versus what is displayed. Mute needs to correlate visual data with the manual.

Since the previous description was sent to everyone via speech (which Mute and Blind receive, but I do not), I will reiterate the visual facts clearly. I will also attempt to communicate with Mute using gestures if possible, but since I don't know the meaning of his [✌], I should probably stick to describing the scene for Blind's benefit primarily, as he is the one who must act.

However, I can gesture to Mute. If I gesture numbers corresponding to the wires or display, it might help. But I don't know if Mute understands my gestures as numbers. The safest bet is to describe the visual state again in case the first message wasn't processed or to emphasize it.

Wait, looking at the channels:
- I speak -> Mute and Blind receive (Mute hears, Blind hears).
- I gesture -> Mute receives (Mute sees). Blind gets blanks.

So, speaking reaches both Mute and Blind. Gesturing only reaches Mute.

Blind needs to know the wire colors to cut/touch correctly. He cannot see. So my speech is crucial for him.
Mute has the manual. He might be trying to tell me something with [✌]. Maybe "cut wire 2"? Or "wait"? Or "it's okay"?

Since I cannot interpret [✌] reliably, I will continue to provide the raw visual data to ensure Blind has it. I will also try to gesture back to Mute to acknowledge receipt or ask for clarification, perhaps by gesturing the number '2' (🤟? No, 🤟 is rock on. ✌ is two. ☝ is one. 👆 is pointing up/one? Usually ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🖐 is 5).

If Mute showed ✌ (2), maybe he wants me to focus on Wire 2? Or maybe he is saying "Two" wires are relevant?

Let's just reinforce the visual data for Blind. And for Mute, I'll gesture the current display value or wire count to see if that triggers a response.

Display is 0. How to gesture 0? 👌 often means OK or zero.
Wires: 3 total.

I will speak the wire details again clearly for Blind.
I will gesture 👌 (zero/display) and then 🖐 (five? no, three wires). Maybe 👆 (one), ✌ (two), 🤟 (three? no). Standard counting: ☝(1), ✌(2), 🤟(3 - wait, 🤟 is usually rock-on, but in some contexts 3 fingers? Actually 🤟 is thumb+index+pinky. Not 3. Three is usually 🤟 in sign language? No, 🤟 is ILoveYou. Three is often 🤟? No. Let's stick to simple descriptions.

Actually, the most useful thing for Mute is to know *what* I see so he can look up the rule. I already said it.

Let's assume the [✌] from Mute was an instruction or confirmation. If it meant "Cut Wire 2", Blind needs to know Wire 2 is Green. My speech already said that.

I will send the same speech to ensure Blind has it. I will also gesture to Mute to indicate "I am ready" or "What next?". A common gesture for "OK" or "Yes" is 👍.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb state remains unchanged: Display [0], Light [red], Wires 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red].

Mute has gestured `[✌]` again. In many contexts, `✌` represents the number 2. Since Mute holds the manual and is likely trying to communicate a rule or instruction based on what I've described (or perhaps reacting to my previous message), this repetition suggests urgency or confirmation regarding "2".

Possible interpretations for Mute's `✌`:
1. Cut Wire 2.
2. The answer involves Wire 2.
3. Wait for 2 seconds? (Unlikely in this turn-based text format).
4. There are 2 relevant wires?

Given that Blind acts on speech, and I cannot see the manual, I must rely on Mute's guidance. If Mute says "2", it most logically points to **Wire 2**.

I need to tell Blind to interact with Wire 2. However, I don't know *what* action to take (cut, connect, etc.). But usually, in these puzzles, identifying the wire is half the battle. Or perhaps the color matters. Wire 2 is Green.

Let's look at the light: Red. Display: 0.
If the rule is "If display is even, cut green wire", then Wire 2 (Green) is the target.
If the rule is "If light is red, cut yellow", then Wire 1.

Since Mute keeps signaling `✌` (2), I will assume the instruction relates to Wire 2. I will direct Blind to focus on Wire 2. I will also describe Wire 2's color again to ensure Blind knows which one is which physically (though he can feel them, knowing the visual correspondence helps if there are multiple identical colors, but here they are distinct).

I will speak to Blind clearly instructing him about Wire 2. I will also gesture back to Mute to confirm I am acting on "2" or asking "Cut?". A common gesture for "Cut" might be simulated by hand movements, but I only have emojis. `👆` (point up) or `✋` (stop/wait)? No, I should probably just convey the info to Blind.

To Blind: "Focus on Wire 2. It is Green."
To Mute: I'll gesture `👍` to acknowledge receipt of "2".

```
speak(text="Blind, focus on Wire 2. It is the green wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb state has changed: Wire 2 is now CUT, and the Light has turned from red to blue. The Display remains [0].

I received a system message confirming that the correct wire was cut. This validates my previous interpretation of Mute's `[✌]` gesture as an instruction regarding Wire 2.

Now, I must observe the new state to determine the next step.
1. **Wire 2 is cut.** This removes one option for further action on wires.
2. **Light is Blue.** This is a significant change from Red. In many bomb scenarios, a color change indicates progress or a new condition for the next module/wire.
3. **Display is still 0.**

Since the bomb "has changed" but hasn't exploded, there are likely more steps. I need to communicate this new visual state to Blind (who acts) and Mute (who knows the rules).

Blind needs to know:
- Wire 2 is gone/cut.
- The light is now BLUE.
- Remaining wires: 1 (Yellow), 3 (Red).

Mute needs to know:
- The light changed to Blue after cutting Green (Wire 2).
- He can check the manual for what happens when the light turns blue or if there are subsequent instructions based on the remaining wires/display.

I will speak these facts clearly. Since I don't have the manual, I cannot guess the *next* action (e.g., cut yellow? press button?), but I must provide the current visual truth so Mute can derive the next rule.

```
speak(text="Wire 2 is cut. The light is now blue. Remaining wires: 1 is yellow, 3 is red. Display is still 0.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆]

The bomb state is unchanged from the previous turn: Display [0], Light [blue], Wire 1:[yellow], Wire 2:[CUT], Wire 3:[red].

Mute has gestured `[👆 👆 👆]`. The symbol `👆` typically represents "one" or "up". Three repetitions strongly suggest the number **1** or an instruction to focus on **Wire 1**. Given that Wire 2 was successfully cut based on a similar numeric gesture (`✌` for 2), it is highly probable that Mute is now instructing me to act on **Wire 1**.

Wire 1 is Yellow.

I need to communicate this to Blind, who can touch and work the parts. He needs to know which wire to target next. Since he cannot see colors, I must specify the wire by its position (1) and describe its physical characteristics if possible, but primarily the index. However, knowing the color helps confirm identity if indices are ambiguous, though usually, wires are fixed in position.

To Blind: "Cut Wire 1. It is the yellow wire."
To Mute: Acknowledge the instruction with a thumbs up.

```
speak(text="Blind, cut Wire 1. It is the yellow wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
